topicTitle: Core Debate Principles, Syllogisms & Rebuttal Strategies

documents.title: Toulmin Model of Argumentation
documents.summary: The gold-standard rhetorical framework for constructing robust, persuasive debate points.
documents.evidence: Every strong argument requires 6 interconnected components: Claim (the statement being argued), Grounds/Data (empirical evidence and facts), Warrant (the logical link connecting data to claim), Backing (support for the warrant), Qualifier (degrees of certainty), and Rebuttal (preemptive address of counter-arguments).
citations: Stephen Toulmin, 'The Uses of Argument', Cambridge University Press

documents.title: Four Pillars of Collegiate Rebuttals (AREI Framework)
documents.summary: Proven framework for dismantling an opponent's case: Assertion, Reasoning, Evidence, Impact.
documents.evidence: To effectively neutralize an opposing point, a debater must not simply state that the opponent is wrong; they must challenge the validity of the premise, identify unstated assumptions, introduce conflicting empirical data, and compare the net magnitude (impact) of both sides.
citations: World Universities Debating Championship (WUDC) Adjudication Manual
